nodes.label: run[] as the execution key that never existed
nodes.norm_label: run[] as the execution key that never existed
nodes.description: executePlan() needs tasks[].run[]; the key is in no template, no plan, and no test, so an --execute run performed zero task steps and only skip_if probes ran.

nodes.label: Determinism split: high at validating, near zero at executing
nodes.norm_label: determinism split: high at validating, near zero at executing
nodes.description: Plan validation scored 9/10 and integrity gates 9/10, while execution scored 2/10 and small-task scope 1/10.

nodes.label: Documented-but-unread plan fields
nodes.norm_label: documented-but-unread plan fields
nodes.description: files, idempotency_key, verify_exit and defaults.on_precondition_fail were documented in SKILL.md and never read by the runner.

nodes.label: Block-style run: breaks the plan YAML parser
nodes.norm_label: block-style run: breaks the plan yaml parser
nodes.description: A 2-task plan written as run: with block-style items parsed as tasks=5 with three 'task with no id' errors; only the flow style run: [{...}] worked.

nodes.label: Loose skip_if: a text probe accepted as a behavioural check
nodes.norm_label: loose skip_if: a text probe accepted as a behavioural check
nodes.description: skip_if: grep -q 'Plan Publish Gate' <source file> exits 0 and plan-mark-done ticks the task, although the string may only sit in a comment.

nodes.label: Green CI proves no contract
nodes.norm_label: green ci proves no contract
nodes.description: 202 tests passed and bun run ci was green while the doc-runner gap was live, because validate-skill.mjs had no check comparing which fields the runner reads against which the template declares.

nodes.label: Schema-runner contract: export RUNNER_CONTRACT_KEYS and assert them in the template
nodes.norm_label: schema-runner contract: export runner_contract_keys and assert them in the template
nodes.description: One contract test -- every key executePlan reads must appear in the template -- would have caught the original finding on its own.

nodes.label: Bounded path produces no plan file at all
nodes.norm_label: bounded path produces no plan file at all
nodes.description: The determinism surface is inverted relative to risk: the most-used Bounded path writes no plan document, so nothing there can be validated; only Architectural has a runner.

nodes.label: Prose steps are the handoff point where the LLM substitutes commands
nodes.norm_label: prose steps are the handoff point where the llm substitutes commands
nodes.description: 'One step equals one command' is advice, not a check: the agent must read prose, extract a command, and run it.

nodes.label: coerceScalar strips quotes without processing escapes
nodes.norm_label: coercescalar strips quotes without processing escapes
nodes.description: A real parser bug found only because the agent's own plan was executed: a backslash reached the shell doubled and the step failed silently as an exit mismatch.

nodes.label: Retracted claim that rendered SVG lacks title/desc
nodes.norm_label: retracted claim that rendered svg lacks title/desc
nodes.description: The false claim reported to the user was that rendered SVG carries no <title>/<desc>; it was retracted after a re-test showed both tags present, wired via aria-labelledby.

nodes.label: a11y gate reads the rendered SVG, not the Mermaid source
nodes.norm_label: a11y gate reads the rendered svg, not the mermaid source
nodes.description: validate-skill.mjs now checks the rendered SVG for title/desc plus aria wiring, because a source-only regex passes even when the render drops the wiring.

nodes.label: No hosted runner: GitHub Actions frozen to manual on free-tier quota
nodes.norm_label: no hosted runner: github actions frozen to manual on free-tier quota
nodes.description: The push and pull_request triggers on main were removed so every push stops burning Actions minutes, with the revert written into the workflow header.

nodes.label: Validate only the changed Mermaid block instead of re-rendering all 26
nodes.norm_label: validate only the changed mermaid block instead of re-rendering all 26
nodes.description: Rendering 26 blocks through a headless browser is the expensive part; the 25 unchanged blocks were proven byte-identical to HEAD so only the 1 new block needed a render.

nodes.label: Contract check split into its own ~30ms command
nodes.norm_label: contract check split into its own ~30ms command
nodes.description: bun run contract:check is separated from the full render, with a negative control: replacing run: must fail and the tree must be clean afterwards.

nodes.label: Grandfather existing loose skip_if so a new hard error does not break old plans
nodes.norm_label: grandfather existing loose skip_if so a new hard error does not break old plans
nodes.description: 6 loose skip_ifs in 3 plan files were allowlisted with written reasons because turning the warning into an error would have broken plans that already existed.

nodes.label: Determinism is only real where the runner actually reads the key
nodes.norm_label: determinism is only real where the runner actually reads the key
nodes.description: Because run[] existed only as prose, the skill was very good at refusing to run a nonsensical plan and had no mechanism at all for running a sensible one.

nodes.label: Fields the runner never reads are a documentation claim, not a contract
nodes.norm_label: fields the runner never reads are a documentation claim, not a contract
nodes.description: 4 of the 6 documented fields were never read, so the documentation described a contract the runner did not implement.

nodes.label: A text-presence probe proves the string exists, not that the behaviour works
nodes.norm_label: a text-presence probe proves the string exists, not that the behaviour works
nodes.description: The lint message spells out why a grep over a source or doc file is loose: the word can sit in a comment, and the runner accepts the exit 0 with no cross-check.

nodes.label: A green suite with no contract check is vacuous
nodes.norm_label: a green suite with no contract check is vacuous
nodes.description: 202 passing tests coexisted with the live doc-runner gap, so the test count was not evidence of the contract.

nodes.label: The largest hole sat in the most frequently used path
nodes.norm_label: the largest hole sat in the most frequently used path
nodes.description: The Bounded path writes no plan document, so the determinism surface is inverted relative to where the risk actually is.

nodes.label: The most important anti-drift rules are also the softest
nodes.norm_label: the most important anti-drift rules are also the softest
nodes.description: Subagent-first, the 10-subagent floor, chunking and the parent diff audit are all prose 200+ lines deep, while the most repetitive rule, Mermaid, is machine-checked.

nodes.label: The agent's own plan being executed is what surfaced the parser bug
nodes.norm_label: the agent's own plan being executed is what surfaced the parser bug
nodes.description: The coerceScalar escape bug only appeared once the new run[] path executed the very plan that implemented it.

nodes.label: One failed tool call is not a finding
nodes.norm_label: one failed tool call is not a finding
nodes.description: A single grep returning empty was mistaken for absent tags; the conclusion was drawn from one failed tool, which is the error AGENTS.md rule 3 warns about.

nodes.label: A source regex cannot prove the render
nodes.norm_label: a source regex cannot prove the render
nodes.description: validate-skill.mjs only regexed the Mermaid source, so it passed while never checking that the rendered SVG actually carries the aria wiring.

nodes.label: Every push burns free-tier Actions minutes
nodes.norm_label: every push burns free-tier actions minutes
nodes.description: The user reported the free package quota drains fast, so the push and pull_request triggers on main were removed and the local path became the only path.

nodes.label: Rendering every Mermaid block through a headless browser is the expensive part
nodes.norm_label: rendering every mermaid block through a headless browser is the expensive part
nodes.description: The cheap path was chosen because mmdc rendering is what costs, so the agent separated which blocks actually changed before spending the browser.

nodes.label: A check that has only ever passed is indistinguishable from one that does nothing
nodes.norm_label: a check that has only ever passed is indistinguishable from one that does nothing
nodes.description: The contract check was sabotaged by renaming run: to runx: so it could be seen failing before being trusted.

nodes.label: A new hard error breaks every plan that predates it
nodes.norm_label: a new hard error breaks every plan that predates it
nodes.description: Turning the loose skip_if warning into an error would have broken 6 existing probes, so they were grandfathered with written reasons.
